summary: Pulaski County tree-top 'Crow's Nest' lookout; a 1937 notice calls it abandoned, a 1947 survey describes a steel tower; now marked removed.

facts.design: Crow's Nest in a tree top (1937 notice); steel tower with an enclosed wooden observation platform (1947 survey)
facts.status_note: Marked 'Removed' on the Central US Lookouts page, which gives no date. The 1937 abandonment and the 1947 survey do not agree. No source read describes the site now.

events.note: June 1937 Rolla Herald notice quoted on the page: the tower has been abandoned and its territory is to be divided between the Texas and Roby towers.
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description of a steel tower with an enclosed wooden observation platform. It does not fit the 1937 abandonment notice, and the page does not reconcile the two.

notes_for_editor: Single source: the Central US Lookouts page for Baldridge. It quotes a June 10, 1937 Rolla Herald notice and a 1947 Coast and Geodetic Survey station description. The two conflict. The 1937 notice says the tower was abandoned; the 1947 survey describes a standing steel tower at the same station. Either a later structure replaced the tree-top tower or one account is wrong. The page does not settle it, so it is left unresolved. The survey's '50 FEET HIGH' could refer to the tower or the platform, so no height is recorded. The page gives no build year, so no built event is recorded. The survey's directions were not checked against the brief's coordinates (37.6226, -92.0719). The Roby page on the same site quotes a 1938 CCC newspaper calling Roby 'the first tower built in Missouri'; not used here. Brief record: county, agency and status 'gone' match the page. No corrections proposed.
